doc: Directory where the input files are located. This is injected by the application and should not be set by the user.
Number of threads used by the application
Target number of vertices relative to input number.
Envelope thickness relative to the bounding box

Thickness of a tube around the open boundary of the input, relative to the bounding box diagonal. When positive, the boundary is not frozen: collapses may move it, as long as every boundary edge that descends from the input's boundary stays within this distance of the input's boundary edges, and a collapse between a boundary vertex and an interior one keeps the boundary vertex where it is. Holes and slits narrower than the tube can close when use_link_condition is false. Boundary that a collapse opens away from the input's is not judged. Negative (the default): every vertex of the open boundary is frozen.
Use sample envelope instead of exact one.
Throw exception if the output does not fulfil the desired criteria. No output will be generated.

Require the link condition before collapsing an edge. When true a collapse cannot change the topology, which also means it cannot create non-manifold edges or vertices. When false those collapses are allowed -- TriMesh represents the result, and any duplicate triangles the collapse produces are merged -- so the mesh can usually be simplified further.

Merge input vertices closer than this fraction of the bounding box diagonal. 0 merges only exactly coincident vertices; a negative value merges nothing. Needed for formats that carry no connectivity, such as STL, which otherwise arrive as a disconnected triangle soup.

Refuse a collapse that would stretch an edge past this fraction of the bounding box diagonal (edges of the input already longer than it are not held to it). Flat regions otherwise coarsen into triangles as large as the region, whose sampled envelope checks cost their area in eps^2 and serialize the end of the pass. 0.2 is four times the default target edge length of tetwild and simwild (length_rel 0.05). 0 or negative: no limit.
